Series-parallel resistor networks: total current (3 reduction steps)

Bank PHY2-DC-SPRTC3-10292026 · created 10-29-2026 · 30 problems

Isomorphic numerical problems. Each item is a different series-parallel topology of a single battery and resistors; the student reduces the network to an equivalent resistance and applies Ohm's law to find the total current. The topology (and hence the reduction sequence) changes between items, not only the numbers.

Problem 1 — (E) 10.00 A

Question. Determine the total current supplied by the battery of the circuit shown.

Reduce the circuit

1. R3 and R4 are in parallel: 1/R34 = 1/10.00 Ω + 1/10.00 Ω, so R34 = 5.00 Ω

2. R34 and R5 are in series: R345 = 5.00 Ω + 1.00 Ω = 6.00 Ω

3. R1, R2 and R345 are in parallel: 1/R12345 = 1/12.00 Ω + 1/4.00 Ω + 1/6.00 Ω, so R12345 = 2.00 Ω

Work back to the individual parts

1. The battery sees R12345 = 2.00 Ω, so the total current is I = V / R = 20.00 V / 2.00 Ω = 10.00 A.

2. R1, R2 and R345 are in parallel (R12345), so each branch has the same voltage 20.00 V; each current is V / R (0 A through an open branch).

3. R34 and R5 are in series (R345), so each carries the same current 3.33 A; each voltage is I × R (0 V across a wire).

4. R3 and R4 are in parallel (R34), so each branch has the same voltage 16.67 V; each current is V / R (0 A through an open branch).

- 0.54 A: Student adds every resistor as if they were all in series.

- 5.00 A: Student reports the current through R2 (one branch) instead of the total.

- 15.43 A: No single mistake - a number close to the largest option, so a lone large value is not a giveaway by size.

- 10.00 A: Correct.
